newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia issues air pollution warning.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia issues air pollution warning.

text.p: Air pollution in Malaysia has reached worrying levels and is probably due to forest fires in neighbouring Indonesia, officials said on Monday.

Skies around Kuala Lumpur and other parts of the country have been hazy over the past couple of weeks, probably because of forest fires on Indonesia's Sumatra island which lies across the Malacca Strait, officials said.
Government officials advised the public to refrain from outdoor exercise and schools have been told to limit outdoor activities.
"We do not want students to be exposed to the bad conditions...," Deputy Education Minister Fong Chan Onn was quoted by the national Bernama news agency as saying on Monday.
Fong said a Japanese-inspired indoor exercise programme would be introduced as an option.
Health Minister Chua Jui Meng said although the health ministry was not empowered to suspend outdoor sports, it hoped players would protect themselves with masks or other devices.
He also urged the public to stay indoors as much as possible.

A Malaysian Environment Department survey of air conditions in Kuala Lumpur and 16 other cities and major towns in Malaysia on Monday found the air in the capital and 13 other places to be "moderately healthy".
Two towns were classified as "unhealthy" while only one was rated as "healthy".
The haze has been particularly thick over northern Malaysia, where on Sunday an airplane race was cancelled in the city of Ipoh due to poor visibility.
Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad, in remarks at the weekend, offered to help pay the costs of putting out the Indonesian forest fires.

In 1994, smoke from coal and forest fires raging in Sumatra and Kalimantan, the Indonesian part of Borneo island, blew across Southeast Asia, shrouding Malaysia, Singapore and other parts of Indonesia for several months.
